what is worship?.title: What is Worship?
what is worship?.base:
Aawdubillahi mina shaytana rajim Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim Alhamdulillahi saani ilkhalqi alaquli akmali nizam wa ahsani kawaam Alwadi ala shiaifi ajdaril maqam wa arfaqi masaam wassalatu wassalamu 'alal mu'ayyidi abla ghil kalam Muhammadinil mabruth sallallahu alaihi wa ala alaihi wa salam Lihidaa yatikaa Fati Anam ila subulis salaam wa ila madalla yali wala yam Walhamdulillah Alladhilam yattakhiz waladan walam yakunlahu Sharikun fil Mulk walam yakunlahu wal yumina zullay wa kabbir hu taqbirah Walhamdulillah Alladi anzala ala Abdhil kitab walam yaja Allahu aywaja Alhamdulillah Alladinahmaduhu wa nastaainuhu wa nastaqfirhu wa nu'minubihi wa natawakkalu alai Wa na'udubillahi min shururi anfusina wa min sayyi ati 'aamalina man yahdihillahu fala mudillala wa man yudlilhu fala hadi Allah Wa nashadu an la ilaha illallah wahtahula sharikala Wa nashadu anna Muhammadana Abdullahi wa rasulih Arsalahullahu ta'ala bilhudawadeen al-haq li yozhirahu aladdinikulli wa kafabillahi shaheedah Wa nashhadu anna mawlana ali ibn Abi Talib wasiyihu wa waziru Fasallallahu alayhim wa ala alayhim wa salim hum tasliman kathiran kathira Allahum mala 'ilmalana illama alamtana inna kaantal ali mulhakeem Allahumma alimna bima yanfa'na wa yanfa'na bima alamtana Allahumma inna na'udhubika min Ail min la yanfa wa min qalbin la yaksha wa min aainin la tadma wa min nafsin la tashba Fa'amma baadi akkullu subhana wa ta'ala fi kitaabihil kareem baada akkulla a'udhubillahi mina shaytana rajeem bismillahir rahmanir rahim Rabbish Rahli Sadri Wa Yasirli Amri Wahlul Iqdatam mill Lisani yafqahu Qawli Allahum masabitna ain dalmauti bila ilaha illallah wallahum majaal naamin Alladhina amanu amil salihat wa tawa sau bil haq wa tawa sau bis sabr ameen ya rabbil alameen As-salamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu. In the last session, I talked about the word 'ilah' and its various flavors and meanings. We learned that when the definite article 'the' or 'al' in Arabic, when it gets applied to 'ilah', it becomes 'al ilah'. And both of those words then fuse together to form 'Allah'. So, all the various meanings of ilah then become exclusive for the one that we call Allah. That's what the Al does. So now, if I take the meaning of ilah as a powerful entity that demands submission, then Allah becomes the one, the only one for me.

Right? He becomes al-ilah for me. The only one I deem worthy of my submission. He becomes the only one I must be completely loyal to. Because there is no one more powerful than Him. And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in reality. And the day He says be, it becomes. His word is the ultimate truth and He has all dominion on the day the trumpet will be blown. He is the knower of the unseen as well as the seen. And He is wise and He knows everything. And then the same formula applies to the rest of the meanings of Ilah. If we take the meaning of Ilah as seeking protection and refuge, then Allah is the only one I exclusively turn to for protection and refuge in desperate times.

If I take illah in the meaning of love, then Allah becomes the only one I choose to be passionately in love with. He is the only entity, the only deity that I choose to be completely obsessed about. For all the infinite favors that He bestows upon me, Knowing well that I am an extremely ungrateful and unworthy creature, He does not hold back in bestowing His favors upon me. Wa atakum min kullima sa altumuhu wa in ta'udu na'amatallahi la tahsuha innal insana lazaluman kafura And He gave you of all that you asked for. And if you try to count the blessings of Allah, you will never be able to count them. Indeed, no doubt about it, man is an extreme wrongdoer, a disbeliever, an ungrateful being. Now, if I take the meaning of ilah in the sense of wallaha, of astonishment, then Allah becomes the only one whose glory and whose magnificence astonishes me. I realize that even when I set out to understand Him, when I venture to recognize Him, I do so with the realization that His loftiness will exhaust my limited capabilities of comprehension and understanding. I will be dumbfounded every single time I attempt to approach Him.

Because there is just nothing that is comparable to Him. And there are no words that can express His glory. If the sea were to become ink, In order to write the words of my master, indeed the sea would be exhausted before the words of my master would be finished. Even if he brought something similar to the oceans to assist, the words of my master cannot be captured. The praise of my master cannot be captured. So that's Walaha. Finally, if I take ilah in the meaning of the one that I lean on for support, then Allah becomes the only one that I choose to lean on. He becomes the only one I choose to put my entire weight of all my spiritual burden on for support. Because His support is the only support that matters. In yansurakum Allaha falaagaalibalakum If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you.

And if He forsakes you, then who is there after Him that can help you? And in Allah, let alone the believers put their trust. So, in other words, there are all these different meanings these various rivers of knowledge that flow out of the word ilah and they all then become exclusive. They all converge into one entity when it reaches the al-ilah or Allah. But the real question is what do we get out of the union of all these meanings of ilah? So if Allah is the only powerful entity deserving submission, if Allah is the only one capable of providing refuge and protection, if Allah is the only one worthy of passionate love and obsession for my thoughts, and if Allah is the only one who astonishes me, astounds me, if Allah is the only one I choose to lean and depend on, Then the union of all these meanings of ilah with its exclusivity of Allah, making Him Allah, what does the union of these meanings produce for me? What does all of this mean to me? What does this make Allah to me? They make Allah worthy of my worship. They make Him worthy of my ibada.

This is why He created me. And I did not create jinn or the humans except that they should worship me. And this is why He says that. Because the sum of all these meanings of ilah, they make him worthy of my worship. This is why every single day, in every single namaz, I say, Iya ka nabudu wa iya ka nasta'in. It is only you that we worship, and it is only you that we seek help from. This concept of Al-Illah, what it leads us to is the idea of worship, the idea of Ibada. And the one we worship is called Maabud. We are the Abd and Allah is our Maabud. Now, what is worship? The word Ibada is commonly translated as worship, right? But linguistically speaking,

![](images/154/60534835-e6af-4fc4-8820-31a58bca68fb.jpg)

The word ibada actually means a combination of two things. It means to worship and it also means to obey, both at the same time. They're not interchangeable like many other words in the English language. No. Both meanings of worship and obedience are embedded inside this one word of ibada in the Arabic language, in classical Arabic. Together, They both mean Ibadah. You cannot take one meaning out of this word. It is worship and it is obedience. But generally, when we think of the word worship, what comes to our mind? The five prayers, fasting, paying Zakat, performing Hajj, right? These are all different forms and the rituals of worship.

![](images/152/5e2c8227-d756-43cf-9baa-783172ee5603.jpg)

So it is worship. But these are the rituals of worship. But what happens is that we think that's it, and we stop at all of those activities. And that's the point that I want to highlight today. The problem with this translation of the word ribada exclusively in the meaning of worship is that it does not necessarily include the concept of obedience. Especially an obedience that stems out of love. That is critical to understand. That is extremely important to understand. Worship is a love-based obedience. Because the word obedience, it can have a very negative connotation to it, right? Because people can be forced into obedience. Children are often bullied into obedience by the use of either threats or violence.

So it is possible for obedience to have a very negative emotion attached to it. But this is not the kind of obedience that we're talking about here when we say Ibadah. Ibadah is an obedience that comes naturally from the appreciation of all these various meanings of ilah that we learned. When we choose to love Allah passionately, when we choose to become obsessed about Him, when we are completely devoted and loyal to Him, when we completely trust Him and lean upon Him, When we're totally impressed and amazed by His loftiness, His greatness, His magnificence, when we know that we can always unconditionally turn to Him for protection and refuge, then the natural outcome of the sum of all of these love-based emotions is obedience. So remember that Ibada is an obedience that stems out of love. It is a lover's obedience to make the beloved happy. And this is why Allah created us. And this is why He gave us this ability to love. He did not create us and desire disobedience from us. He allows disobedience. His magnificence enables this capability of disobedience within His creation because disobedience is a product of free will.

which is called Khizlaan. But Allah is not content with it, because disobedience is completely contrary to the concept of love. You know, there's a poet by the name of Mahmud al-Warraq, and in one of his poems he says, You disobey Allah and then you feign the love of God? This is an impossible and unknown kind of logic. Had your love been sincere, you would have been obedient. Because a lover is always obedient to the one he loves. So, it is the nature of love that we want to obey the one that we love. In another one of his poems, he says, . You know, a woman once asked someone about the state of this person who loves her with this burning passion. Ashik is the one who is burning up with passion. Right?

They say, Dawa ul aishq ali tisal. The only cure for aishq is to be connected with the beloved, to be in the embrace of the beloved. So, she's talking about this man, she's asking about this man who loves her, and she's inquiring about his love for her. And this is something that lovers do, right? They want to know, they inquire from others about how much their beloved loves them. So, she asks this man, Lillahi sifhu, walatanqus walatazidi. For Allah's sake, describe him to me and don't stint in your description and don't exaggerate. In other words, you know, I want to know the truth. I want to hear the truth. So, this man, he says, Lawkana rahlil mauti bid duma'i. If your lover thought that he would die from thirst, Waquti qifan wurud al ma'i lam yaridi. And if you said don't touch that water, he wouldn't touch it.

So her lover knows that he is going to die of thirst, but if the woman said don't touch that water, he wouldn't touch it. He'd rather die than disobey. So the point of that, what he's emphasizing there is that the nature of love is obedience. So the more you love Allah, the more you will want to obey Him. So Ibadah to Allah has these two concepts embedded within it: worship and obedience. Both of which stem out of this passionate love for Him and not from some kind of forced compulsion or coercion. And to put this in practical terms, to give you an example, let's say, you know, we are about to pray in 15 minutes, right? Let's say it's Fajr time. And so we have to pray. We have to do our Ibada. We have to go through the ritual of prayer.

Now, what kind of Ibada is prayer, Salat? Is it worship or is it obedience? It's worship, right? But then from Fajr all the way up till Zuhr, we will not be worshipping him through this ritual of prayer, but if we are sincere in our love for him, we will be doing what? We will be obeying him. We will be in a state of obedience with him. Because it is the dream and the desire of every lover to make their beloved happy. And so the beauty of this word ibada is that it covers the entire spectrum of love, putting us in a constant state of worship. You see, when we are performing the ritual acts of Salat, we are in a state of ibada. But then when we are in between two prayers, by being in a state of obedience, we are still in the state of ibada. You see, this is why

the concept of ibada is so comprehensive in Islam we are constantly in a state of worship if not through the formal rituals then through obedience so what this means is that if you go in the morning and earn a halal income through your job that is an act of obedience that is an act of ibada when you go to school and you sincerely accomplish the purpose of education, you're in a state of ibadah, you're worshiping. When you love and respect your elders, when you are kind to your siblings, when you're generous to the needy, when you're courageous in the face of temptations, no matter what you do, as long as you're in a state of obedience and servitude to Allah , anything and everything that you do becomes an act of ibadah. It becomes worship. It turns into worship. Going to the toilet becomes Ibadah. Imagine that. When you go to the toilet to relieve yourself, if you obey the commands of Allah to cover your head and feet and seek His protection and recite all those duas, you're in a state of Ibadah. So you can see that this concept of worship of Ibadah is really incredible in Islam. And may Allah give us all the strength and Tawfiq to become his obedient slaves and to fulfill the purpose of our creation. Wa akhiruda wanaan alhamdulillahi rabbil alameen wassalatu wassalam aala Rasulahi Saidira Muhammadin Khatimin nabi yeen was sayyid al-mursaleen wal akhihi wa wassi yaalib nabi Talib asharafil wassi yeen wa 'alal aimmatimin zariatima taibinatahirin wassallam alayhi majma'in al-fatiha

the womb of afterlife.base:
Audubillahi mina Shaytan regime Bismillahu Rahmanur Rahim Allahumma saliya ala Sayyidina Muhammadin Wa ala Ali Sayyidina Muhammadin kamasalayta wa salamta wa barakta wa rahimta wa tarahamta ala Ibrahim Wa ala Ali Ibrahim fil alamina Inna Kahmidu Majid Rabbish Rahli Sadri wa yaserli Amri Wahlul Uqtata millisani of Kahukawli Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu Now that we understand these meanings of Rab and Rahman and Raheem, now that we understand these terms, I want to share with you a beautiful spiritual representation that Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala has created for us through the example of the womb, the Rahem. To quickly reiterate these terms, Rab is a combination of six things in classical Arabic. The definition is a Rabbuhu al-Maliku was Sayyidu al-Murabbi al-Murshid wal-Muna'im al-Qayyim So a Rab is an owner and he is the one with complete authority over its property He is the one who nurtures his creation guides it benefits it by bestowing generous and undeserving gifts upon it and he is the one who maintains it So this is who Allah is, right? That's His primary role with His creation of Rabb. And all His other attributes, they basically center around and they stem from His Rabul biyya. So if someone asks, who is Allah? The answer to that question is Allah is Rabb. Now, as for His nature, His nature is Ar-Rahman and Ar-Raheem. So the manner in which he executes or the way he carries out the functions of his Rubul biyya, it is through intense and consistent love, compassion and mercy.

So now that we understand these concepts, I want to share this example that Allah has created for us through the womb. You know, by studying the womb, we can actually understand a lot about our master's plan for us. Just by studying the relationship of the womb with its fetus. Because this womb, it is the first rub of the fetus. And it demonstrates the exact same principles of Rahmaniyya and Rahimiyya in its interaction with it. This is why there is a Hadith in which Rasulullah , he said This world is a womb for the afterlife. In other words, the story of our lives in this world, it tells a tale about the kind of life that we're going to have in the afterlife because This world, this dunya that we're living in is the womb or access the womb and we are the fetus in that womb. And just as the brief and temporary residence in a womb is actually preparation for this worldly life, Our stay in this temporal world is nothing more than a short duration of preparation for the afterlife. Now, if you look at the Rahem, the womb, you'll see all six principles of Rubbiya at work. It has ownership and it has authority over the embryo, right?

It nurtures the embryo, it helps the embryo grow and develop into a fetus. So the womb is Malik, it is Sayyid and it is Murabbi. Then we see that the womb, it bestows these priceless gifts upon the fetus to the development of its eyes, its nose, its ears, hands, feet, the heart, the intellect and all of its internal and external organs. So we can see that the womb is also the Muna'im, the bestower of gifts. We also know that the womb, it manages the entire development process of the embryo from its conception all the way until it is fully developed. So the womb is also ayam. So we can see that the womb, it actually acts as the very first physical rub that we come in contact with. And this very first act, it actually demonstrates the design of how Allah created this mechanism. It demonstrates the act of Rububiyya by carrying out all six functions of the definition of the word Rab, right? Malik, Sayyid, Murabbi, Murshid, Munhayim, Qayyim. Now, what happens once the baby is delivered into this world?

Who is the baby handed over to? It is handed over to its loving mother who becomes the next immediate Rabb of that baby. Not the father, the mother. It's the mother that becomes the next Rabb. Why? Because she feeds it. She takes care of it. There is this transference of Rubbiya that takes place. The mother now takes ownership of the baby. The mother now takes authority over it. The mother assumes the responsibility of nurturing it, helping it grow and develop, teaching it, guiding it, setting it to purpose, showering all these gifts and blessings upon it. She becomes the one who maintains that baby's sustenance in all its various forms, physical, emotional, psychological.

So we can see that our mothers become the next immediate Arab Right after the Rububiya of the womb, the Raham, it's completed. Now father is also a Rab, but his Rububiya gets executed through the mother. You see, the father always uses the mother as a means for her. He facilitates her functions of Rububiya. That's the role of the father, but the primary caretaker of the child is always the mother. So now let's study this Hadith to better understand the underlying principles that are at work. So Rasulullah , he said, . This temporal world is the womb of the afterlife. So let's examine the fetus and the womb of its mother. Is it the womb actually doing all the work? Or is it the mother doing all the work behind the scenes and letting this womb act as an intermediary between herself and her child?

Is it the womb or the mother? We know it's always the mother, right? The mother is the one taking care of the baby's needs. She is the one eating all the right things. She is making sure she doesn't bump into things so that her baby doesn't get hurt. She's the one getting all the ultrasounds done, taking all those painful but necessary blood tests, all those injections. So she is the one actually suffering for the baby. Baby is living comfortably in the womb, but it's the mother doing all the work, right? The mother is the one doing all the hard work all along. But from the perspective of the fetus, who is doing all the work? The womb, not the mother. You see, the fetus has absolutely no knowledge of its mother.

All it knows, all it recognizes, all it understands is the womb. If I ask the fetus, who do you think is feeding you? Who do you think is nurturing you, taking care of you, sustaining you? Who is doing all the work that is necessary for your health and development? What will the fetus reply? The womb. The fetus has absolutely no knowledge of the existence of its mother. You see? What mother? Where's the mother? I don't see a mother. All I see is the womb.

There is no mother. It's just cause and effect. When I tell this fetus, no, no, it's not the womb, it's the mother. She is the one feeding you. She's the one taking care of you. This womb is only an intermediary. It's a means. And the fetus says, you know, what are you talking about? It's the umbilical cord that's feeding me. That's what gets me this blood that is carrying all the nutrients. I get fed by that, the umbilical cord. The umbilical cord is responsible for my development.

There is no mother. And so I explain, no, no, there is a mother. She is all around you. You are within the love, the care, the concern, and the mercy of your mother. This womb wouldn't exist if she didn't exist. And this womb that you're in, it's actually temporary. This is not the world you were created for. Believe me, this world is filthy, it is dark, it is immensely constricted. There is an amazing and a beautiful world that exists outside this womb that has been created just for you. And that world is so magnificent that you cannot even imagine its glory right now within this womb. Trust me, this womb is filth compared to that world. So if you think this womb is kind and merciful to you, let me tell you, it doesn't even compare to the love and the mercy of your mother.

Because your mother is going to take care of you in the next world. She will shower you with so much love that you have absolutely no idea. You cannot even imagine that while you're in this womb. But the fetus says, what are you talking about? I am really really happy here. Everything I need is being taken care of for me right here. Why do I need to have another world? I don't know why you keep talking to me about this mother and another world and an afterlife. There is no mother. There is no world outside this womb. You're crazy. Okay show me.

Show me this world that you keep talking about. Show it to me right now. I want to see it. Prove to me that there is another world. Prove to me that there is actually a mother. I'm not gonna believe you unless and until I see that world and until I see that mother. And I say, I can't show it to you right now, but I promise when you transition out of this world, this womb, you'll see both of them. Oh, so now I'm supposed to trust you. I'm supposed to trust your belief system, your intellect? What if you're wrong? Now this is us with Allah in this world. There are so many of us denying the existence of the mother living in the comforts of this womb, of this dunya.

So now, I begin this logical path of explanation and I say, look, you have been given these eyes, but there is so little to see here. You've been given these ears, but there's so little to hear. You've been given taste buds, but there is so little to taste here. You have a nose with this magnificent ability to smell, but there's not a single fragrance here. You have arms, you have feet, you have all these amazing gifts, but you cannot benefit from them within this womb. So think about it. These are of no use to you inside this womb, which means there must be another world that is out there, a world where you will be able to use and benefit from these gifts. Think about it. Your only purpose in this womb, in this world, is to draw your sustenance from your mother and develop these organs. In other words, you're here so that you can prepare them for the next world where you will actually be using them, where you will actually benefit from them. But does the fetus understand that?

No. It doesn't. To the fetus, the concept of another world and the existence of a mother is just ridiculous. Just as the concept of a God and an afterlife is absurd to so many of us. So now what happens? This fetus continues to live in its ignorance and its arrogance until the nine months complete. Now what happens? Contractions begin. The fetus starts panicking. What's going on here? What's happening? This is what was promised to you.

I told you this day would come. I told you this world is temporary. So now with those contractions, this beautiful world of the fetus, this magnificent world it was living happily and comfortably in, it starts crumbling around it. It starts falling apart all around it. Now, isn't that exactly the description of the Day of Judgment? When the earth is shaken up with its earthquakes. And the earth discharges its burden. And man says, What is wrong with this world? What is wrong with this earth? Yaw ma izin tuhaddisu akhbaraha bi anna rabbaka o haalaha On this day, it will report the news of which your master has commanded it. Yauma izin, yasduru naasu ashtatan liyurao a'malahum.

On this day, people will separate out, and they will be shown the results of their deeds. Fa man yaamal misqala zarratin khairan yara. So, whoever did an atom's weight of good will see it. It dies in the womb in order to be born again in the next world, you see. Its death in the womb results in its creation in this world. That's what the word intaqal means. It comes from naqala, which means a transference. It also means a copy or a replica. That's what naqala means, a copy or a replica.

Why? Because the next world is going to be a copy, it is going to be a replica of the first. If you did good in the world, in this world, you will find good in the next world. If you did evil in this world, you will find evil in the next world. It's going to be a replica, it's going to be a copy. If the fetus has not properly developed its eyes, its ears, its brain, its limbs in the womb of its mother, it is going to suffer the consequences of that in the afterlife of this dunya. SubhanAllah. So now this temporal world of the fetus is destroyed and it comes into this huge world that he was informed about. this world that was promised to him in the womb. He is now forced into this world, this afterlife that he chose not to believe in. And then, as soon as it's out of the womb, who is the baby handed to? The mother.

Subhanallah. The mother that he said did not exist, the mother he denied his entire life in the womb. So you can see that the fetus goes through the exact same confusion of the seen and the unseen while it's in the womb of its mother. That's so many of us go through in this life. The fetus that accepts the rububiya of its mother through the womb comes out fully developed and is now capable of enjoying all the benefits that the afterlife has to offer, which is this physical world for the fetus. But the fetus that rejected the rububia of the womb, it comes out underdeveloped, blind, deaf, mute, physically challenged, mentally challenged, incapable of benefiting from the joys and pleasures that this world has to offer. We are all going through this exact same process in life. Why? Because Ad-Dunya Rahmul Akhra this world is the womb for the afterlife. And what do we say?

who left you behind in this world and when that little girl who was buried alive will be asked for what sin were you killed this is the day where Allah will exact justice this is the day of justice not this world not this dunya that we're living in that day all the deeds will open up And when the book of deeds will be made public, wa iza samaa ukushitaat And when the sky will be stripped away, wa izal jaheem usoa'irat And when that hellfire is set ablaze, wa izal jannatu uslifaat And when the paradise is brought near, alimat nafsun ma ahdarat Every soul will know what it has brought with it.
